analyst_view.overall: Arouca (5th, 20 points, only 8 conceded in 11 games) host Rio Ave (17th, 7 points) on matchday 12, and Rio Ave coach Vasco Seabra returns to the club he left in October when Rio Ave paid his release clause. Record says Seabra arrives under pressure: Rio Ave have lost four in a row including the Taca exit at Vianense and are back in the relegation zone, and he is considering changes to the starting XI to give the side new energy. Centre-back Andreas Ntoi has served his two-match ban and may be back in the squad (A Bola), which restores Rio Ave's usual defence rather than changing what the numbers assume. Arouca's Miguel Puche and Rio Ave's Nelson Abbey and keeper Cezary Miszta are already counted as out; captain Marios Vrousai went off injured in the cup and this week's reports give no update on him. Referee Diogo Rosa (5.7 cards a game in three games) is already counted, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 1.8 for Arouca against a Rio Ave defence that let in 13 in its last six (already counted), and they already take Puche out for Arouca. Ntoi's likely return helps Rio Ave's back line while Vrousai's status is unclear, and Seabra's planned changes are not named yet; nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 5.6 to 4.1 for Arouca, already lifting Arouca a little because Rio Ave have conceded 36 corners in their last six. Rio Ave need a win more than Arouca and could push their full-backs on, but they have lost four in a row playing that way; I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already adding a little for referee Diogo Rosa (5.7 a game, small sample) and Rio Ave's booking rate, and trimming Arouca because Rio Ave have drawn few fouls lately. Seabra's return adds some edge and Rio Ave are in the drop zone, but there is no history of bad blood between the clubs, so I stay at 5.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.6 shots and already take about 14% off Rio Ave, who managed only 51 shots in their last six, and add about 7% to Arouca against a Rio Ave side that has allowed 93. Seabra knows Arouca's players well and may change his XI, but no names are out, so I stay at 23.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target, with small form changes already in. Arouca's defence has been one of the league's best this season, which the numbers see, and Rio Ave's possible return of Ntoi only restores their usual back line; I stay at 8.5.
